chunks: Then give advice concerning the traders and those with crafts, and advise well of them:

the settled among them, the one whose wealth is in transit, and the one who exerts his body, for they are the sources of benefits, and the means of supplying needs, and they bring them from distant places and markets, in your land and sea, your plains and mountains, and where people do not easily gather for their locations, nor do they dare to go to them,
for they are peaceful, from whom no revolt is feared, and a truce, from whom no treachery is feared. Check on their affairs in your presence and in the outskirts of your land.
ai.seo_question: How should a governor manage and advise traders and artisans according to Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: In this foundational text of Shia political economy, Imam Ali (AS) elevates merchants and artisans from mere economic actors to essential pillars of societal stability, describing them as 'peace' (silm) whose disruption would cause unrest. This instruction reflects the historical context of Egypt’s trade routes, emphasizing that the governor must actively protect these mobile professionals who bridge remote regions and urban centers, ensuring their welfare to maintain economic flow and social order.

en.sayed-ali-raza: (6. Traders and Industrialists) Now take some advice about traders and industrialists. Give them good counsel

whether they be settled (shop-keepers) or traders or physical labourers because they are sources of profit and the means of the provision of useful articles. They bring them from distant and far-flung areas throughout the land and sea, plains or mountains, from where people cannot come and to where they do not dare to go,
for they are peaceful and there is no fear of revolt from them, and they are quite without fear of treason. Look after their affairs before yourself or wherever they may be in your area.
